claims.text: The funding supports attendance of Genetics Society junior scientist members at genetics research conferences.
There are three streams for the funding: (A) attendance at Genetics Society/SIG meetings, (B) attendance at non-Genetics Society meetings, and (C) attendance at virtual conferences.
Scheme (A) is for undergraduate, Master’s, and PhD student members, and postdoctoral scientist members within six years of their PhD viva.
Schemes (B) and (C) are for PhD student and postdoctoral scientist members within six years of their PhD viva.
Schemes (B) and (C) are open to members with a UK base wishing to attend conferences outside of the UK and to non-UK-based members wishing to attend a conference in the UK.
A maximum of one grant per two years will be awarded for applications to Scheme (B) or (C).
Applicants must present a poster or give a talk at the conference.
Supervisors providing support letters must be current members of the Genetics Society and include their membership number.
Grant recipients will be asked to write a short report that may be published in the Genetics Society Newsletter.
Grants up to £200 are available for travel and accommodation for Scheme (A).
Grants of up to £500 are available for travel, accommodation, and registration for Scheme (B).
Up to two Scheme (B) grants per year will be co-sponsored by the Adelphi Genetics Forum and provide up to £750.
The Adelphi Genetics Forum co-sponsored award is only open to registered PhD student members who will take up the award before their PhD graduation date.
Grants of up to £300 are available to cover registration costs for virtual conferences (Scheme C).
Applications should be submitted by bi-monthly deadlines: 1st day of February, April, June, August, October, and December.
Applications should be made by logging into the mySociety membership portal.
The conference must take place AFTER the application deadline.
For Scheme (A) meetings, applications should be submitted online before the registration deadline of the meeting.
Queries regarding the application process can be directed to theteam@genetics.org.uk.

claims.text: The grant covers travel and accommodation costs for field-based genetic research projects.
The grant is funded by income from the journal Heredity.
Research funded by this grant should produce results suitable for publication in Heredity.
The deadline for the next round of applications is February 1st, 2024.
Awards are available up to £2,000.
All members of the Genetics Society can apply if they are studying or working in the UK, or intend to carry out fieldwork in the UK.
Students can apply as soon as they become Society members.
Other applicants should be a Society member for at least one year.

The grant will support costs directly associated with the field component of a research project, including travel, accommodation, subsistence, consumables for pre-processing, and travel/accommodation/subsistence for an essential field assistant (who must also be a Society member).
Equipment essential for gathering data in the field may be eligible, but should not total more than one third of the funds applied for.
Fieldwork that is an essential part of a study and already budgeted for will not be covered.
Costs associated with lab procedures, salary for fieldwork, and fieldwork outside the UK (if not working/studying in the UK) will not be covered.
Attendance at conferences is not covered.
Applicants must either live or work in the UK or intend to carry out their fieldwork in the UK.
Students require a supporting letter from their supervisor, who must also be a member of The Genetics Society.
Applicants must be completing the fieldwork themselves.
Only one application per research group is funded in a twelve-month period.
An individual can only claim one Heredity Fieldwork Grant in any two-year period.
Applicants need to explain why their student funding does not cover the intended fieldwork.
A short report must be submitted within two months of completing fieldwork for potential inclusion in the Genetics Society newsletter and website.
Applications are made online via the Genetics Society Grants application site.
Deadlines are quarterly, at midnight on February 1st, May 1st, August 1st, and November 1st.

Applications must include a completed online GS Funding Application Form, a recent CV detailing relevant fieldwork experience, and a supporting statement from a supervisor who is a member of The Genetics Society.
The Genetics Society aims to notify decisions within one month of application deadlines.
Applications should be submitted at least 3 months in advance of the fieldwork start date.
